title: The Nature of Ethical Duty in Deontology
text:
Deontological ethics posits that the moral worth of an action is determined by whether it adheres to a set of rules or duties, regardless of the consequences. Central figures like Immanuel Kant emphasized that morality stems from rational necessity and universalizable maxims.

The core concept involves acting out of duty, meaning the motivation for the action must be respect for moral law rather than inclination or predicted benefit. This structure requires individuals to test potential actions against the Categorical Imperative, ensuring they could become universal laws without contradiction.
Therefore, an act is considered morally right only when it serves as a dutiful commitment to principle itself.
